title: Baltor / Teleon — standards interoperability
principle: They standardize where context lives; Baltor governs whether it's true.
stance: Adopt open formats at the EDGES (ingest + emit) and govern ABOVE them. Every adopted standard is a projection; the governed object stays the core. We add the assurance the formats themselves don't carry — verification, freshness/CDC, earned source-authority, portable receipts. Proprietary data-gravity layers are declined, not adopted.

standards.name: Open Knowledge Format (OKF)
standards.governance_added: verification, freshness/CDC (a reconstructed log.md), source-authority, receipts — none of which OKF mandates
standards.note: Import an OKF repo into governed objects; export governed objects as conformant OKF with our assurance in the frontmatter. Round-trip lossless. Candidate projection (OKF is v0.1 / single-vendor).

standards.name: Native format preservation (JSON / CSV / Markdown)
standards.governance_added: a governed sidecar (lineage + receipts) alongside the byte-identical native output
standards.note: Detect a customer source's native shape, freeze it, and reproduce the same format on the way out — assurance travels in a sidecar, never by mutating the source.

standards.name: FollowTheMoney (FtM) entity schema
standards.governance_added: verified source-authority + freshness + receipts + topics promoted only from governed flags (never inferred from free text) — assurance FtM itself does not carry
standards.note: Map governed entity records -> FtM EntityProxy (Aleph-loadable; id=lei-<LEI> else dc-<sha1>; schema adopted, library optional via a PyICU-free pure-Python serializer). Imported as a candidate standard from the DueCare entity-intelligence reference (2026-06) — same adopt-the-schema-govern-above pattern as OKF.

standards.name: W3C PROV-JSON
standards.governance_added: a baltor_governance facet so the provenance is portable into any PROV consumer
standards.note: Emit governed lineage events as a W3C PROV-JSON document (entities/activities/agents + used/wasGeneratedBy).

standards.name: OpenLineage RunEvent
standards.governance_added: a baltor_governance custom facet on the run + every output dataset
standards.note: Map a lineage event to an OpenLineage RunEvent (spec 2-0-2) — portable into any OpenLineage backend (Marquez, Atlas, Purview).

standards.name: W3C Web Annotation
standards.governance_added: the annotation binds a verified claim to the exact source fragment it was earned from
standards.note: Emit a claim→source binding as a W3C Web Annotation (body + target + selector).

standards.name: JSON-Patch (RFC 6902)
standards.governance_added: each patch carries the governance under which the change was promoted (no silent edits)
standards.note: Emit a before→after context change as an RFC-6902 JSON-Patch with its governance.

standards.name: JSON-LD @context (schema.org · DCAT · SKOS · PROV-O · DPV · SPDX · Croissant · MCP)
standards.governance_added: hub terms map to the public vocabularies so emitted records are linked-data-resolvable
standards.note: A JSON-LD @context maps hub terms to the standard vocabularies; renderers emit standards-conformant records.

standards.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
standards.governance_added: MCP is the transport; the governance/receipts ride above it as a candidate gateway, never truth
standards.note: MCP is the universal transport every platform adopts; we ride it for tool/context access and govern above it.

standards.name: AWS Bedrock Knowledge Bases
standards.reason: a proprietary managed-retrieval SERVICE with no open knowledge format — adopting it is lock-in, not interoperability. We consume open inputs and ride above any serving layer.
standards.note: Declined as a format; can be wrapped as one candidate retrieval backend behind a port, never a source of truth.

standards.name: Databricks Unity Catalog (managed)
standards.reason: UC-OSS + Delta catalog-commits are open, but the managed brokering AUTHORITY (data gravity) is the lock-in. We ingest the open table/lineage signals, not the managed authority.
standards.note: Open table/lineage edges are candidate inputs; the managed catalog authority is declined.

standards.name: Microsoft Purview / Fabric control plane
standards.reason: Purview emits OpenLineage→Atlas (which we consume), but the catalog/identity control plane (Entra/Fabric) is proprietary lock-in. Ride the open lineage edge, decline the control plane.
standards.note: OpenLineage edge is a candidate input; the proprietary control plane is declined.
